core_obligations: Record the two immediate implications from the first formulation to the second and from the second to the third (proof lines 6913-6915).

Pass from the third formulation to the fourth: for affine test schemes and morphisms into the base change, compute the relevant fibre product as the base change of the product along the diagonal, and read off that it is quasi-compact in the quasi-separated case and an affine scheme closed in that product in the separated case (proof lines 6917-6926).

Pass from the fourth back to the third: read the same computation backwards, choose the affine test schemes so that they form an etale covering of the base change, and conclude that the diagonal is quasi-compact, respectively a closed immersion (proof lines 6928-6950).

Pass from the third to the fifth: use the presentation of the target, write a member as a colimit of affine formal subschemes, observe that the diagonal for the member is the colimit of the diagonals for the pieces, and conclude by testing after base change along affine schemes into the square (proof lines 6952-6972).

Pass from the fifth to the first: write the fibre product square for the coproduct of the members of the presentation and transfer the property from its left vertical arrow to the right one by descent for representable transformation properties (proof lines 6974-6981).
proof_roadmap: Third to fourth by computing the fibre product over the diagonal (proof lines 6917-6926).
Fourth to third through an etale cover of the square (proof lines 6928-6950).
Third to fifth by a colimit argument over the presentation (proof lines 6952-6972).
Fifth to first by descent along the covering (proof lines 6974-6981).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of formal algebraic spaces and any of the separation axioms, the lemma states the equivalence of five formulations: the axiom itself; the axiom after base change to every scheme; after base change to every affine scheme; the statement that the affine base changes are of the corresponding type as formal algebraic spaces; and the axiom for the members of one presentation (statement lines 6884-6911). The first two implications are immediate once the stability of the axiom under base change is granted. The proof then supplies three genuinely different arguments. It passes from the third to the fourth by computing the relevant fibre product as a base change of the product of two affine schemes along the diagonal, and reading off that the result is quasi-compact, respectively an affine scheme with a closed immersion into that product (proof lines 6915-6926). It passes back from the fourth to the third by reading that computation backwards, using that the fibre products of an etale covering by affines form an etale covering of the square, to conclude the corresponding property for the diagonal (proof lines 6928-6950). The passage from the third to the fifth uses the presentation of the target, writes each member as a filtered colimit of affine formal subschemes, notes that the diagonal for the member is the colimit of the diagonals for the pieces, and concludes by testing after base change along affine schemes into the square, which is exactly what the factorisation statement for such colimits allows (proof lines 6952-6972). The final implication produces a fibre product square for the coproduct of the members of the presentation and uses the descent statement for representable transformations to transfer the property from the left vertical arrow to the right one (proof lines 6974-6981). The claim is H3: four implications are proved by four independent mechanisms -- a fibre product computation with the diagonal, its converse through an etale cover of the square, a colimit argument over a presentation, and a descent along a covering -- and each is displayed.
